stories.title: University of Leeds report
stories.body: The University of Leeds report explores the social case for CMIs, considering, amongst other things, how resident investors’ views of their council change post investment.
stories.headline: Headline finding: 55% of local investors say they trust councils that issue CMIs more than those who do not.

stories.title: Green Finance Institute report
stories.body: The Green Finance Institute report explores the financial case for CMIs. Using historic PWLB borrowing and historic saving rates, as well as interviews with council treasury managers, it identifies credible use cases for CMIs today and a pathway for growing the model to scale.
stories.headline: Headline finding: the report suggests that, at scale, total cost of capital for councils could get consistently close to the Gilt Rate.

stories.title: New Abundance website
stories.body: We recently launched a new version of the Abundance website. The platform is now 100% focused on councils and has more space to explain how local government works and its role in making communities better. We have also updated the look and feel of the platform to make it relevant to funding a broader range of the capital programme and, in turn, making CMIs more attractive to a broader cross section of the community. Please let us know what you think.

stories.title: CMIs deliver local government funding below Gilt Rate
stories.body:
During the March to June window, £1.70m was raised across the period with an average weighted saving of 81 basis points on the PWLB Certainty Rate, effectively below the Gilt Rate.

The window was priced 24 hours before the start of the Iran war, which then drove a steep increase in the cost of borrowing for councils. This demonstrates the diversification and resilience benefits of growing a citizen investor base for local government, generating the same benefits NS&I provides central government.

fields.body:
There are four launch windows each year, with a fixed interest rate set per window. Upcoming launch windows are 30 November 2026, 1 March 2027, 1 June 2027 and 1 September 2027.


Councils can launch an offer at any point during a window and, thanks to institutional lender backing led by Unity Trust Bank, all loans launched are fully funded.
